description: Fickling has a detection bypass via stdlib network-protocol constructors
how_introduced: AI-assisted code in 19e828d26b248a4a39fcee2643306a6cd78dbb76 materially contributed to the CVE: it expanded `UNSAFE_IMPORTS` with a new network-module section, but still omitted `smtplib`, `imaplib`, `ftplib`, `poplib`, `telnetlib`, and `nntplib`, the exact gap closed by the fix. The broader incomplete-blocklist design predates AI involvement, but this Claude-coauthored commit rewrote the relevant network coverage and left the stdlib network-protocol constructor bypass in place.

bug_commits.author: Dan Guido
bug_commits.message: Integrate recent PickleScan bypasses into unsafe imports detection

agent_verdicts.reasoning: This Claude-coauthored commit added the `UNSAFE_IMPORTS` network section (`webbrowser`, `aiohttp`, `httplib`, `http`, `ssl`, `requests`, `urllib`, `urllib2`) in `fickling/fickle.py`, and the fix later appends the missing stdlib protocol modules directly into that section. Because `Global`/`StackGlobal` create `ast.ImportFrom(module=...)` nodes and `analysis.py` treats stdlib constructors as likely safe unless their module is in `UNSAFE_IMPORTS`, leaving out `smtplib`, `imaplib`, `ftplib`, `poplib`, `telnetlib`, and `nntplib` preserved a detection bypass. The screening hypothesis is directionally right about the omission, but slightly imprecise: this commit did not create `UNSAFE_IMPORTS` from scratch; it incompletely expanded the existing blocklist in the exact area the fix changes.
